join_order.notes: Iterate lt_ids and walk CSR offsets+rowids to enumerate ~5000 ml rows

join_order.build: tv_title_bitset (size 2528312) from title__kind_id CSR at tv_kind_id
join_order.probe: for each ml row: test t1_id and t2_id membership
join_order.notes: Single pre-build; reused for t1 and t2 checks

walk movie_companies__movie_id[t1_id]; require company_id in cn1_us_bitset
join_order.notes: Capture min(cn1.name) over matching company_ids for this t1

data_structures.tv_title_bitset: bitset(2528312) over title row index (id-1), built from title__kind_id CSR slice at tv_kind_id
data_structures.mc_lookup: offsets_only movie_companies__movie_id (used twice per ml row: t1, t2)
data_structures.mi_idx_lookup: offsets_only movie_info_idx__movie_id (used twice per ml row: t1, t2)
data_structures.aggregation: six per-thread running MIN slots (cn1.name, cn2.name, mi_idx1.info, mi_idx2.info, t1.title, t2.title); final merge across threads

indexes.purpose: drive: enumerate ml rows for lt_ids
one-time build of tv_title_bitset for tv_kind_id
per-movie company lookup for mc1 and mc2
per-movie rating lookup for mi_idx1 and mi_idx2

string_compare.mi_idx2.info < '3.0': byte-wise lex compare against literal '3.0' (memcmp with min(len,3) then length tiebreak); not numeric

parallelism.strategy: morsel_driven over lt_ids CSR rowid slice (the ~5000 driver rows)
parallelism.notes: Each thread maintains private 6-way MIN slots; merge at end. Pre-built bitsets and dim scalars are shared read-only.

notes: Driver is the CSR over movie_link by link_type_id: only ~3 of 18 link types qualify, yielding ~5K ml rows.
Pre-build cn1_us_bitset and tv_title_bitset once before the parallel driver loop.
For each ml row, perform cheap title filters first (tv_title_bitset for both t1 and t2; year window on t2) to prune before walking mc/mi_idx CSRs.

MIN semantics: a row contributes its t1.title and t2.title once a single qualifying (mc1, mc2, mi_idx1, mi_idx2) tuple exists. We accumulate MIN over all matching companies and ratings as required by SQL MIN semantics (each matching combination contributes independently, but MIN collapses them).
No EXISTS/anti-join; no bloom filters needed. All joins resolve via direct array / bitset / offsets walks.
